LESSON: SOCIO- ECONOMIC PRACTICES OF EARLY HUMANS - EARLY - MIDDLE - LATE

Grade: SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade 9
Subject: SOCIAL STUDIES
Strand: People, Population and Relationships
Topic 3.1: Socio- Economic Practices of Early Humans - Early - Middle - Late
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 6

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Socio- Economic Practices of Early Humans - Early - Middle - Late, part of People, Population and Relationships in SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade 9 SOCIAL STUDIES.

Key inquiry question: How are Socio- economic practices of early humans impact to the modern society?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Socio- Economic Practices of Early Humans - Early - Middle - Late together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Digital literacy: learners use digital technology skills as they use available digital devices to find out and view various types of tools

used by early humans during the Stone.

● Creativity and imagination: learners undertake group tasks and gain new perspectives as they discuss in groups the various types of

tools used by early humans during the Stone Age period.

Values:
● Unity: Learners respect opinions of others as they brainstorm on socio-economic practices of early humans during the Stone Age

period.

Link to other learning areas:

● Kenya Sign Language and English: learners apply language skills as they brainstorm in groups on socio-economic practices of early

humans during the Stone Age period.

● Agriculture and Nutrition: learners will gain knowledge on farm tools as they discuss in groups the various types of tools used by early

humans during the Stone Age period.
